description: Confirmed Asterinas defects (REPRODUCED or MASKED). Drop-in for Specula's docs/known-findings/asterinas.json. Read only during bug confirmation, never in analysis, spec generation or hunting.

entries.title: ext2 durable write prefix returned as EFAULT

also_seen_in.finding_id: analysis-report T-1, CR-1; modeling-brief T-1, CR-1

entries.mechanism: The page-cache write fault arm marks an up-to-date page dirty and returns the error, the (ostd::Error, usize) conversion drops the copied count, and ext2 write_at returns a count only on success, so the shared offset and size stay behind data that is already durable.
entries.contract: write(2): a transfer interrupted by a faulting user page after a positive prefix returns the short count, and the committed data, the count, and the offset agree.
entries.observed: Asterinas commits the prefix to the ext2 page cache (and to disk under O_DIRECT) but returns -1/EFAULT and leaves the offset and size unchanged.

entries.title: ramfs size publication before an empty or zero-progress write
entries.mechanism: RamInode::write_at publishes size, blocks, mtime and ctime and resizes the page cache to offset+len before the fallible page_cache.write, with no rollback on a copy fault and no early return for a zero-length write.
entries.contract: write(2): a zero-length write to a regular file has no other effect, and a write that copies nothing must not extend the file beyond the write start.
entries.observed: Asterinas ramfs grows the file to offset+len (or beyond, for a seeked offset) after a zero-length write past EOF or a write that faults before copying any byte.

entries.title: Vectored I/O releases the offset lock between iovecs
entries.mechanism: do_sys_readv/do_sys_writev call the scalar file.read/file.write once per iovec, and InodeHandle takes and releases the shared offset lock per scalar call, so a competitor on a dup'd descriptor can commit between two iovecs of one vector call.
entries.contract: readv(2)/writev(2): a vector transfer on one open file description is atomic with respect to other I/O through that description (Linux holds f_pos_lock for the whole call).
entries.observed: Asterinas lets a concurrent read or write on a dup'd descriptor land between two iovecs of one readv/writev (79 to 98 of 100 rounds torn at SMP=2).

entries.title: A copied read prefix is erased by EFAULT reporting

also_seen_in.finding_id: analysis-report T-1, CR-1; modeling-brief T-1, CR-1

entries.mechanism: read_fallible copies the prefix and returns (PageFault, copied); the error conversion drops copied; Vmo::read propagates the error after the copy; InodeHandle advances the offset only on Ok, so the next read re-delivers the prefix.
entries.contract: read(2): a fault after a delivered prefix returns the short count and advances the offset by it.
entries.observed: Asterinas copies the prefix into the buffer but returns -1/EFAULT with the offset unchanged, so the next read re-delivers the same bytes.

entries.title: ramfs/exFAT reads copy beyond the reported EOF prefix
entries.mechanism: RamInode::read_at and ExfatInode::read_at compute the EOF-limited length but hand the caller's unlimited writer to the page cache; the cache is page-aligned and Vmo::read clips only against capacity, so bytes past the returned count are overwritten (or a fault past EOF becomes EFAULT).
entries.contract: read(2): the kernel writes only the returned number of bytes into the caller's buffer and leaves the rest untouched.
entries.observed: Asterinas ramfs and exFAT overwrite the caller's buffer past the returned count (zeros up to the page-cache capacity), even when the read returns 0 at EOF.

entries.title: Failed append advances the shared file offset
entries.mechanism: InodeHandle::write assigns *offset = size for O_APPEND before the fallible write_at and only skips the += len on error, so a write that faults at byte zero leaves the shared offset at EOF.
entries.contract: write(2) with O_APPEND: a failed write must not move the shared file offset; the offset follows committed progress only.
entries.observed: Asterinas moves the shared offset to EOF on an O_APPEND write that fails with EFAULT, so later reads through the description return EOF.

entries.title: Empty Segment conversion dereferences an unowned first frame
entries.mechanism: Segment::slice accepts start == end and returns a zero-length segment holding no reference; both TryFrom<Segment<dyn AnyFrameMeta>> conversions unconditionally do Frame::from_raw(range.start) and a dyn_meta() virtual call on a frame the segment does not own.
entries.contract: ostd frame API: Segment<M> -> Segment<dyn AnyFrameMeta> -> Segment<M> is the identity, and a segment never reads metadata of frames it does not own.
entries.observed: An empty end-boundary slice makes the conversion answer from a neighboring frame's metadata (identity broken, typed frames accepted as USegment); at 4c1fdd1e4 an uninitialized slot killed the kernel.

entries.title: IOMMU teardown frees frames before IOTLB invalidation
entries.mechanism: unmap_dma_remap removes the IOMMU PTEs per page but issues no IOTLB invalidation, and DmaCoherent/DmaStream drop then frees the frames, so a device with a cached translation can write into a recycled frame.
entries.contract: DMA revocation: after an unmap returns and its frames are freed, the device can no longer reach those frames (VT-d requires IOTLB invalidation after removing a translation).
entries.observed: Asterinas never invalidates the IOTLB on DMA teardown, so a device wrote 64 bytes into a frame already recycled to an unrelated kernel allocation (QEMU vIOMMU, edu device).

entries.title: Pipe readv/writev return EINTR despite SA_RESTART
entries.mechanism: Pipe reads and writes wait through wait_events and pause_timeout, which return EINTR; only sys_read/sys_write map EINTR to ERESTARTSYS, while do_sys_readv/do_sys_writev return the raw EINTR, so handle_pending_signal never restarts the vectored calls under SA_RESTART.
entries.contract: signal(7): a blocking read/readv/write/writev on a slow device (such as a pipe) interrupted by a handler installed with SA_RESTART is restarted, not failed with EINTR.
entries.observed: Asterinas returns -1/EINTR from readv on an empty pipe and writev on a full pipe after an SA_RESTART handler runs, while scalar read/write restart in the same boot.

entries.title: ramfs snapshots read length before serializing with resize
entries.mechanism: RamInode::read_at reads the file size and computes read_len before taking the page-cache lock, then returns the saved read_len after Vmo::read silently clamps the copy to the current VMO capacity. A concurrent ftruncate or extending write in that gap makes the returned count differ from the bytes delivered, and InodeHandle::read advances the shared offset by the stale count.
entries.contract: read(2)/pread(2): the returned count equals the bytes stored in the buffer, and read advances the offset by exactly that count, even when racing truncate or an extending write.
entries.observed: pread64 of a 4096-byte ramfs file racing ftruncate(fd, 0) returned 4096 while delivering 0 bytes, and read(2) advanced the shared offset by 4096 with 0 or 8192 bytes delivered.

entries.title: exFAT write preparation becomes stale before copy/publication
entries.mechanism: ExfatInode::write_at computes new_size and resizes the page cache under inner.write(), releases the lock, copies under a fresh upread() where Vmo::write silently clamps to the current capacity, then publishes the stale new_size and returns the full count. A competing extending write or truncate in the gap shrinks the cache or overtakes the size.
entries.contract: write(2): a successful write returns the bytes actually stored, and after it returns the file size covers the written range and reads return the written data.
entries.observed: Two racing extending pwrite64 calls on one exFAT file: one returned 4096 after storing 0 bytes and left st_size beyond the cache (reads return 4096 without data), or st_size regressed below an already-successful write.

entries.title: Successful exFAT ftruncate retains the old logical size
entries.mechanism: The public ExfatInode::resize used by ftruncate delegates to ExfatInodeInner::resize, which only updates size_allocated and clusters (size is assigned only when clusters decrease below the old size), and never publishes the logical size itself, so extension and same-cluster shrink leave inner.size unchanged.
entries.contract: ftruncate(2): on success the file length becomes exactly the requested size. Extension reads as zeros and data beyond a shrink is lost.
entries.observed: ftruncate(fd, 1) and ftruncate(fd, 8192) on an empty exFAT file returned 0 with st_size 0, and ftruncate(fd, 2048) on a 4096-byte file returned 0 with st_size 4096 and all 4096 bytes still readable.

entries.title: exFAT regrown holes expose the file's old backing bytes
entries.mechanism: exFAT truncate frees clusters only in the allocation bitmap. A later extending write reallocates them first-fit, PageCache::resize zero-fills only the old partial tail page, and submit_read_bio returns zeros only for pages at or beyond logical size, so hole pages below EOF are read from the reused clusters' old on-disk bytes.
entries.contract: lseek(2)/ftruncate(2): bytes in a gap created by writing or extending past EOF read as zeros until written.
entries.observed: After ftruncate(fd, 0) and a pwrite of one page at 8192 on exFAT, pread of [0, 8192) returned the file's previous 'A' and 'B' page contents instead of zeros.

entries.title: exFAT cold-tail extension re-enters an inode write guard
entries.mechanism: ExfatInode::write_at calls PageCache::resize under inner.write(). For an unaligned old size the extension branch runs fill_zeros on the tail page, which commits an uncached page through the backend, and the exFAT backend submit_read_bio takes inner.read() on the same non-reentrant RwMutex, so the writer deadlocks on itself while holding the fs lock.
entries.contract: write(2)/pwrite(2): an extending write to a regular file returns a count or an error and never blocks forever on a lock held by the calling task.
entries.observed: After remounting exFAT so the tail page of a 100-byte file was uncached, pwrite64(fd, buf, 16, 100) did not return within 10 s and the guest had to be killed by the outer timeout. Cached-tail exFAT and remounted ext2 controls returned 16.

entries.title: epoll copy-out EFAULT loses edge-triggered readiness
entries.mechanism: EpollFile::pop_multi_ready removes a ready EPOLLET entry (Entry::poll returns is_still_ready=false) before do_epoll_pwait2 copies events to user memory. A write_val EFAULT returns with no rollback, and nothing requeues the entry because no new notification arrives.
entries.contract: epoll_wait(2)/epoll(7): an epoll_wait that fails with EFAULT delivers no event, so an edge-triggered event must still be returned by the next valid epoll_wait.
entries.observed: After epoll_wait returns EFAULT for an unwritable buffer, a valid epoll_wait returns 0 while the EPOLLET eventfd is still unread.

entries.title: epoll disables one-shot interest before successful delivery
entries.mechanism: Entry::poll calls Observer::reset_enabled for an EPOLLONESHOT entry while collecting the event, before do_epoll_pwait2 copies it out. An EFAULT leaves the interest disabled, ReadySet::push ignores later notifications, and only EPOLL_CTL_MOD (Entry::update) re-enables it.
entries.contract: epoll(7): EPOLLONESHOT disables the descriptor only after an event is pulled out by epoll_wait. A call that failed with EFAULT pulled no event, so the next valid epoll_wait must report it.
entries.observed: After epoll_wait returns EFAULT, the one-shot interest stays disabled and a valid retry returns 0 until EPOLL_CTL_MOD rearms it.

entries.title: Final close retains dead epoll interest metadata
entries.mechanism: EpollFile keeps an Entry keyed by a weak file reference after the watched file's final close. The only dead-entry cleanup is in pop_multi_ready for ready entries, so a never-ready entry stays in interest and dump_proc_fdinfo keeps printing its tfd line.
entries.contract: epoll(7) Q6: once all descriptors of the watched open file description are closed, the file is removed from every epoll interest list.
entries.observed: After the only descriptor of a never-ready watched eventfd is closed, /proc/self/fdinfo/<epfd> still lists its tfd entry for the life of the epoll instance.

Stage-2 table said Medium, final Stage-3 severity is High. Historical evidence at the pin only. Static read of upstream main bc12195df on 2026-09-24 showed the same code shape. No runtime retest.

entries.title: Consumed timerfd remains ready through the poll cache
entries.mechanism: TimerfdFile::try_read clears ticks with fetch_and(0) but never calls Pollee::invalidate, so Pollee::poll_with keeps returning the cached POLLIN. TimerfdFile::set_time clears ticks the same way (static only).
entries.contract: timerfd_create(2): a timerfd is readable only while expirations are pending. After a successful read consumes them, poll must not report POLLIN and a nonblocking read returns EAGAIN.
entries.observed: After a successful read of a one-shot timerfd, repeated poll calls return POLLIN while the next nonblocking read returns EAGAIN.

repro.how_to_run: Apply the plumbing patch at the pin, copy the test into test/initramfs/src/regression/io/specula/, and run make run_kernel SMP=2 ... SPECULA_INIT="/test/io/specula/run_bug.sh test_bug3_timerfd_cache". See repro/README.md (MC-4 programs use inverted exit codes).

entries.caveats: Runtime evidence covers the read (drain) path through poll only. The disarm and epoll paths come from TLPI-v2 F17, whose probes are NOT_RUN. Cache installation uses compare_exchange_weak, so tests should prime the cache. Some MC-4 programs exit 0 when the bug triggers. Static read of upstream main bc12195df on 2026-09-24 showed the same code shape. No runtime retest.

entries.title: signalfd mask change omits newly eligible readiness
entries.mechanism: update_existing_signalfd only stores the new mask (relaxed store) and nonblocking flag without notifying pollers. SigQueues::enqueue is the only notifier, so an already-pending signal that the new mask admits never wakes the existing epoll registration.
entries.contract: signalfd(2): replacing the mask of an existing signalfd makes it readable when a pending signal is in the new mask, and Linux wakes pollers on the update.
entries.observed: After signalfd4 adds an already-pending signal to an existing signalfd's mask, epoll_wait times out while direct poll and read of the signalfd succeed.

repro.how_to_run: Apply the plumbing patch at the pin, copy the test into test/initramfs/src/regression/io/specula/, and run make run_kernel SMP=2 ... SPECULA_INIT="/test/io/specula/run_bug.sh test_bug5_signalfd_mask_transition". See repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Process-directed signal path only (self-kill with the signal blocked). The debate addendum cites a worktree qemu.log that no longer exists. Challenger output survives in reproduction.md and turn logs. Not the AST-41 binding oracle. Historical evidence at the pin only. Static read of upstream main bc12195df on 2026-09-24 showed the same code shape. No runtime retest.

entries.title: poll times out after timerfd becomes readable
entries.mechanism: do_poll returns Ok(0) directly when Poller::wait (Waiter::pause_timeout) reports ETIME, skipping the count_events rescan it runs after other wakeups, so a timerfd that expired and notified before the timeout decision is reported as a timeout.
entries.contract: poll(2): a return of 0 means the timeout expired before any descriptor became ready. Linux do_poll rescans descriptors before accepting the timeout.
entries.observed: poll returns 0 at the timeout boundary although the timerfd was already readable (observed readable while the poller slept), and an immediate nonblocking read returns a full tick.

entries.title: signalfd epoll readiness binds to the registering thread
entries.mechanism: SignalFile::poll, called from Entry::update in the epoll_ctl caller's context, registers the epoll poller only with that thread's (and its process's) signal queues. A thread-directed signal to another waiter thread notifies only that thread's queue, so the epoll entry is never woken.
entries.contract: signalfd(2): a thread reading a signalfd receives signals directed to itself, and the descriptor is readable to poll/epoll when such a signal is pending, regardless of which thread registered it.
entries.observed: When thread A registers the signalfd and a signal is directed at waiter thread B, B's epoll_wait times out twice while B's direct read of the signalfd returns the signal.

repro.how_to_run: Build the static test into an initramfs (the .nix files need the plumbing patch's initramfs.nix change), build the kernel at the pin with cargo osdk, and boot with qemu -smp 2. See repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Found by code review. The corrected model hunt does not cover it. Kept separate from the AST-41 model oracle, whose trace has a similar shape but no caller-visible outcome. Process-directed signals were not shown to fail. Not reviewed by the Terra review. Static read of upstream main bc12195df on 2026-09-24 showed the same code shape. No runtime retest.

entries.title: epoll_pwait/pselect6 timeout skips deferred pipe readiness
entries.mechanism: Waiter::pause_timeout returns ETIME whenever the timer has expired after wakeup. Pollable::wait_events propagates it without rerunning the readiness closure, and do_epoll_pwait2 and do_poll map ETIME to 0, so readiness that woke the waiter before the deadline is reported as a timeout when the waiter runs late.
entries.contract: epoll_wait(2)/poll(2)/select(2): 0 means no descriptor became ready before the timeout. Readiness that occurred before the deadline must be returned even if the waiter runs after it.
entries.observed: With the waiter delayed past its 200 ms deadline by a SCHED_FIFO writer that wrote the pipe before the deadline, epoll_pwait and pselect6 (and epoll_wait/ppoll on one vCPU) return 0 and an immediate zero-timeout retry reports the pipe ready.

repro.how_to_run: Build test_bugCR-5_wait_mask.c statically into an initramfs for a kernel built at the pin, boot it from a GRUB ISO using cr5-grub.cfg, preferably with one vCPU. See repro/README.md.

entries.caveats: Final SMP=2 trace failed for epoll_pwait and pselect6. The first SMP=2 run exposed epoll_wait and ppoll, and the one-vCPU challenger run failed all four. sched_setaffinity does not migrate threads on this checkout, so one vCPU is the reliable setup. Signal-mask restoration was correct. Static read of upstream main bc12195df on 2026-09-24 showed the same code shape. No runtime retest.

entries.title: ext2 direct-write fault/rollback can leave an earlier BIO live
entries.mechanism: InodeInner::write_direct_blocks submits each mapped run into a local IoBatch and only waits after the loop. A user-copy fault on a later run returns through ?, dropping the batch (no Drop, no cancel) with an earlier BIO in flight, after which write_direct_at rolls back and, for extending writes, frees the blocks the live BIO targets.
entries.contract: An I/O syscall that returns (including with EFAULT) has no outstanding device I/O. Linux iomap_dio_rw waits for every submitted BIO, and IoBatch documents that the caller waits for all records it added.
entries.observed: An O_DIRECT pwrite spanning two non-adjacent runs returned EFAULT while the first run's BIO was still in flight and later published 4096 bytes. No later operation was ever clobbered in 64-round and 32-round probes on virtio-blk and NVMe.

repro.how_to_run: Apply specula-initramfs-plumbing.patch to the pin, place the C files in test/initramfs/src/regression/io/specula/, and boot with SMP=2 and SPECULA_INIT pointing at a script that runs them on /ext2 (and /nvme). Cases A/B COMMIT_WITHOUT_REPORT with C NO_PUBLICATION show the mechanism.
repro.runtime_status: MASKED at 604948581 (01a MC-6, SMP=2): mechanism observed in cases A/B/C, harm not observed in D-G, J, J2

entries.caveats: Masked by backend: the mask is a single-worker FIFO staging queue per device plus the blocking wait_all in zero_new_blocks (a debater correction, whereas turn 1 and the 01a handoff name the in-order virtqueue). The write-after-free shape needs a near-full block group. Linux ext4 also returns EFAULT with a committed prefix, so that return alone is not a contract violation. Drivers reference a removed confirmation worktree.
